findings.anchor: the four scenes, and every version from v19 to v25
findings.problem: The scene art is hand-authored SVG. That lane was abolished on 2026-08-01, in a founder ruling recorded the day he saw hand-drawn SVG scene art one time too many: 'I never want to again.' Art comes from the founder's own generations, from verified legal photography, or from a studio cut PROVED by art-execution-gate. Hand-authored SVG is none of those and art-gate.py has been sitting in the repo the whole time, unrun, ready to say so. Seven consecutive versions of scenery were composed in a lane that does not exist.
findings.fix: Stop. The Art Director owns the shot list and has never been seated on this build. Nothing further gets drawn until there is one.

findings.problem: The compositions are wrong on their own terms, which is what an unseated Art Director costs. Scene 0 is Echigo-Kawaguchi, deep snow country in Niigata, and it is drawn as generic gabled huts - no steep gassho or irimoya pitch, no deep eaves, no snow guards, no dark timber, and a torii placed as decoration rather than at an approach. Scene 1 is a father and child at a neighbourhood curb and it is drawn as pitched-roof houses standing in front of a downtown skyline, which is two settings at once. The streetlamps in scenes 1 and 3 are invented shapes that match no fixture anyone has stood under. None of this was referenced; it was composed from memory by a lens with no art brief.
findings.fix: Art Director writes a shot list per scene naming the real place, the era, and the specific objects that must be in frame. Period Librarian sources reference. Nothing is drawn from memory.
findings.evidence: founder, 2026-09-20: 'those aren't Japanese houses or a village... the street lights look alien... why are houses in the city?'
